items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Chuck Mangione’s first record was made — I don’t know whether Cannon should get credit for that or otherwise — but no Chuck was a damn good player.

ctx.x: Well that’s one thing I loved about his bands is he had, even though it was a quintet or sextet, they had arrangements in there.

Oh they had a very strong sense of arrangements, strong sense of composition in that band. The best way to describe my feelings about Julian Adderley is that I have learned over the years that no matter how close you can become to someone when you are working together, it is extremely difficult to maintain that relationship after the end of the © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

period of working together. Because the circumstances change. I mean you don’t have that regularity because practically you’re always either planning or doing or coming off of a record date when you’re working together. And there’s a great deal of planning together and hanging out together. And when that goes, what you have to recognize is you’re not going to have in most cases, that same kind of closeness. And you have to realize nobody’s mad at anybody necessarily. Sometimes yes, but very often not, it’s just…
